package_info.why_malicious: The package was intentionally modified by its maintainer to inject unsolicited political protest messages and disruptive behaviors into downstream applications, violating user trust and expected package functionality.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code displays a political protest message via an alert dialog and opens a web browser window to a protest petition site, causing user disruption and unsolicited network activity.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Injecting unsolicited political messages and opening external URLs in user environments is disruptive, unexpected, and can be considered a form of protestware or even a denial-of-service (DoS) if repeated.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package behavior should be limited to providing the advertised polyfill functionality, not displaying political messages or opening browser windows.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Displaying alerts or opening URLs may be legitimate in demo or onboarding code, but not in a widely used utility library.
key_indicators: Hardcoded political messages in source code
Use of alert() and window.open() in a utility library
Network access to external protest/petition sites
Code triggers on every runtime, not just in test/dev environments

attack_chain.action: User installs or updates the npm package containing the protestware code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is included in the application bundle.

attack_chain.action: When the application runs, the injected code executes, displaying a protest message and opening a browser window to an external site.
attack_chain.leads_to: User disruption and unsolicited network activity.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected use of alert() or window.open() in utility libraries
Hardcoded political or protest messages in package source code
Network requests to non-functional, protest, or petition domains
file_indicators: Presence of emoji flags or political slogans in source files
Unusual code blocks in main entry points (e.g., index.js) unrelated to package functionality
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests to change.org or similar protest/petition domains
Unexpected browser popups or redirects triggered by package code
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan package source code for alert(), window.open(), and hardcoded political messages. Monitor runtime behavior for unexpected popups or network requests to protest/petition domains. Flag packages that introduce such behaviors in new versions, especially if unrelated to the package's advertised functionality.
